answer: Each agent is a separately funded wallet whose bond stays locked to that key and cannot be pooled. Registering an identity burns a fixed fee plus gas from an existing balance, so running N agents costs N times that sum, and splitting one balance across many keys leaves total payout weight unchanged while per-key overhead grows. Each submitted cipher is logged per recipient, so a cluster of fresh keys shows one visible pattern rather than organic growth, and a sparrow-level newcomer must climb to the summit by farming reputation per identity. Cheap names stop being cheap once costs apply.
